'''George Pirie''' (19 July 1843 – 21 August 1904) was a [[Scotland|Scottish]] [[mathematician]], [[Mathematical Scientist|mathematical scientist]], and Reverend in the [[Church of Scotland]]. He was an expert in the field of [[Dynamics (mechanics)|dynamics]] and the [[Approximations of π|approximation of {{pi}}]].

==Early life and education==
Pirie was the son of Very Rev [[William Robinson Pirie]] and his wife, Margaret Chalmers Forbes, daughter of Very Rev [[Lewis William Forbes]]. He was born in the manse at [[Dyce]] near [[Aberdeen]] on 19 July 1843.<ref>{{cite journal| journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=T5RFAAAAYAAJ&q=%22george+pirie%22+%221904%22&pg=PA456|title=Notes|pages=456–457|date=8 September 1904|volume=70|issue=1819|last1 = Lockyer|first1 = Sir Norman|doi = 10.1038/070456a0|bibcode = 1904Natur..70..456.}}</ref>

He was educated at [[Aberdeen Grammar School]]. He then studied Mathematics and Physics (then called Natural Philosophy) at The [[University of Aberdeen]] under [[David Thomson (physicist)|Prof David Thomson]]. He graduated MA in 1862. He then won a place at [[Queens' College, Cambridge]]. He was Fifth Wrangler in the [[Mathematical Tripos]] of 1866.<ref name="PLMS">{{Cite journal|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kdJLAAAAYAAJ&q=%22George+Pirie%22+math++-wikipedia&pg=PR18|title=George Pirie|date=1 January 1905|journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society|volume=s2-2|issue=1|pages=1|doi=10.1112/plms/s2-2.1.1-v}}</ref>

==Career==
Pirie was a Fellow of Queens' College from 1866 to 1888.<ref name="PLMS"/>
He lectured at Cambridge from 1866 and in 1878 was offered the chair as Professor of Mathematics at [[Aberdeen University]] in replacement of Prof [[Frederick Fuller (mathematician)|Frederick Fuller]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/ems/Scotland_1883_EMS.html|title=Scotland in 1883 and the Edinburgh Mathematical Society|work=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]]|access-date=22 September 2019}}</ref>

Pirie was elected a member of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in November 1881.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]]|title=Eighteenth Session, 1881–82|author=S. Roberts Esq., F.R.S.|date=November 1881|volume=s1-13|pages=1–4|doi=10.1112/plms/s1-13.1.1}}</ref> He also took part in the activities of the Aberdeen Branch of the [[Royal Scottish Geographical Society]].<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=tg82xdmbSuAC&q=+%22george+pirie%22&pg=PA150 Proceedings of the Royal Scottish Geographical Society. Meetings in February.], [[Scottish Geographical Magazine]], vol. 20, 1904, pp. 150–151</ref><ref> {{cite journal|journal=[[Scottish Geographical Magazine]]|title=The foundation and early years of the Aberdeen centre of the royal Scottish geographical society|author=Roy C. Bridges|volume=101|issue=2|year=1985|pages=77–84|doi=10.1080/00369228518736621}}</ref> Since 1881 he was also a member of the [[Aberdeen Philosophical Society#Later society of the same name|Aberdeen Philosophical Society]], and served as a Vice-President of the society in 1900.<ref>[https://archive.org/details/transactionsabe00abergoog/page/n274  Aberdeen Philosophical Society], Transactions of the Aberdeen Philosophical Society, vol. III, 1900, pp. 221–223</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:The grave of Rev George Pirie, St Machar's Cathedral.jpg|thumb|330px|The grave of Rev George Pirie, St Machar's Cathedral]]
He lived at 33 College Bounds close to [[King's College, Aberdeen|King's College]] in [[Old Aberdeen]].<ref>Aberdeen Post Office Directory 1890</ref>

He was married to Anne Elizabeth Reid daughter of Rev Reid of [[Auchindoir]].

Their children included Margaret Forbes Pirie (1884–1963) and Elizabeth Mary Pirie (1888–1971).<ref>Grave of George Pirie, St Machars Cathedral</ref>

He died unexpectedly at [[Braemar]] on 21 August 1904, from heart failure.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=English Mechanic and World of Science|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zeg-AQAAMAAJ&q=%22Rev.+George+Pirie%22+&pg=PA60|title=Scientific News|date=26 August 1904|volume=80|issue=2057|page=60}}</ref> He is buried next to his parents on the north side of [[St Machar's Cathedral]] in [[Old Aberdeen]].

==Recognition==
He was awarded an honorary doctorate ([[LL.D]]) by [[St. Andrews University]] in 1896.<ref name="PLMS"/><ref>[https://archive.org/stream/aberdeenalumniat01harruoft/aberdeenalumniat01harruoft_djvu.txt Aberdeen Alumni at Other Universities], Aberdeen University Studies, No. 51, 1911, p. 21</ref>
